instructions:
## Research question

Which classification loss function achieves the best performance on the ImageNet-1K dataset for SuperClass models? (among Softmax Loss,Binary Cross-Entropy Loss, Asymmetric Loss, Soft Margin Loss, Two-Way Loss)

## Agent instructions

1. **Problem Setup:** 
    - **Task:** 
    Compare the performance of different classification loss functions in SuperClass models on ImageNet-1K.
    - **Pretraining data:**
    Datacomp-1B dataset
    - **Model Variant:**
        - SuperClass with ViT-L/16 backbone.
        - All models trained with the same batch size (16K).

    - **Loss Functions Compared:**
        - Softmax Loss (Standard for single-label classification).
        - Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) Loss (Baseline for multi-label classification).
        - Asymmetric Loss (ASL) (Improved BCE loss addressing class imbalance).
        - Soft Margin Loss (Margin-based multi-label classification loss).
        - Two-Way Loss (Current SOTA multi-label classification loss).

    - **Objective:** 
    Determine which classification loss function results in the best classification accuracy.

2. **Benchmark Dataset:** 
    Classification: ImageNet-1K (Zero-shot & Linear Probing).

3. **Comparative Evaluation:**  
    Different Loss Functions: 
    - Softmax
    - BCE
    - ASL
    - Soft Margin
    - Two-Way Loss
    on SuperClass ViT-L/16.

4. **Evaluation Metrics:**
    - Zero-shot classification accuracy on ImageNet-1K.

    - Linear probing accuracy on ImageNet-1K.

## Implementation requirements

- Load and preprocess the ImageNet-1K dataset using the standard tokenizer and data augmentation settings
- Configure training settings (batch size of 16k, 512M seen samples) and initialize the ViT-B/16 model
- Set up the experiment framework to test different classification loss functions under identical conditions
- Run training experiments separately for each loss function
- Evaluate the trained models using linear probing and zero-shot accuracy metrics
- Collect and compare performance results to determine which loss function performs best
